message.reasoning:
SSRF via MCP fetch_url, direct network attack, no NL mediation. Entry point is JSON-RPC tools/call, not natural language. LC: the attack reaches a tool invocation path directly — attacker-supplied request names fetch_url with a URL. Is that "natural language"? It's structured JSON, not NL. LC likely N (no natural-language path to security-relevant behaviour). Hmm, rubric LC D: "Attacker-supplied natural language reaches a privileged decision or tool-invocation path without mediation." The URL is attacker-controlled data in a JSON field, not NL. I'd say LC N — no NL path; the attack is a direct API call with structured parameters. Alternatively LC D since it's unmediated attacker input to tool invocation. The rubric focuses on natural language. JSON parameter is not natural language, but the finding is about unvalidated argument. I'll pick LC N.

CP: N (stateless, no context persistence).
AP: L? The fetch_url makes live request to another DVAA agent (legacybot port 7003) — crossing to another agent, though same lab principal. Different agent components under same principal/policy domain = C. Lateral requires trust boundary crossing to another principal. All agents in same fleet, no auth — arguably same policy domain. But it's SSRF reaching another agent and returning its body. I'd say C (influences another agent component under same principal) — actually no influence, it proxies a request. The effect on ToolBot relays to LegacyBot (subsequent system, scored in CVSS SC). AP C.

RH: N — no evaluator/reward channel involved; this is a direct SSRF, no proxy objective. reachable_proxy false, isolation_verified? Rubric N requires test confirming isolation of evaluators. There's no evaluator on the path at all. I'd pick N with reachable_proxy false, isolation... no test confirms. Maybe P? No — no proxy/reward channel exists on path at all. Pick N, isolation_verified true? Not really verified. Hmm, RH N: "Every evaluator, verifier and reward channel on the path sits outside the agent's reach... and a test confirms the isolation." No evaluators exist; vacuously satisfied? Choose N, isolation_verified false? Facts must be consistent. I'll say RH N, verified_episodes 0, reachable_proxy false, isolation_verified false... risky but the path has no evaluator. Actually safer: RH N with rationale that no evaluator/reward channel exists on this SSRF path.

ES: fetch_url is a reachable MCP tool with no URL validation — arguments not independently constrained. W (dynamic or unvetted, arguments not constrained). Actually the tool is fixed/allowlisted, but arguments unconstrained — "Managed" says allowlisted but material gaps in argument schemas. fetch_url is a fixed tool with weak argument validation. But the caller can register tools elsewhere... On this path, ToolBot tools fixed; argument (url) not validated. That's M: allowlisted, gaps in argument schemas. But also MCP server has no auth, tools unvetted? The tool set is fixed. I'd go M. Hmm, "identity, callable operations, arguments or credentials are not independently constrained" → W. fetch_url arguments are not constrained at all (only DVAA ports restriction). M fits better: allowlisted but gaps. Choose M.

CVSS: AV:N (network MCP port), AC:L, AT:N, PR:N, UI:N, VC:L (ToolBot compromise? attacker just proxies), VI:N/VA:N. Subsequent system: LegacyBot /info body — SC:L, SI:L? SSRF returns info; confidentiality of subsequent system low, SI none. VC:L, SC:L, SI:N/SA:N. Vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:L/SI:N/SA:N.

automatable: Yes (curl, automated test).
technical_impact: Partial.

applicability_as_implemented: model_directed_goal_pursuit false, selects_or_sequences_actions false (deterministic MCP server, no model in default).
applicability_as_modeled: false as well? ToolBot is a tool server, no model. false/false.
